fieldMarks: Intermediate-sized canid: larger than a coyote and smaller than a grey wolf; females average about 24 kg and males about 29 kg.
Coat usually described as reddish-brown or tawny, but highly variable.
Cannot be reliably told from coyotes or grey wolves by sight; proper identification requires genetic data.
behavior: Lives in family packs; winter pack size in Algonquin Park has been recorded at 9-14.
Preys on white-tailed deer, beaver and moose; some Algonquin wolves travel up to 42 km to follow deer to winter concentration areas.
Dens are usually in conifer-dominated forest near permanent water, in diggable soil such as sand.
habitat: Typically deciduous and mixed forest landscapes of the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence forest region, with abundant prey and low human-caused mortality.
range: Restricted to south-central Ontario and south-central Quebec, with a core in and around Algonquin Provincial Park and smaller, isolated populations elsewhere in central Ontario (e.g. Killarney Provincial Park, Kawartha Highlands) and Quebec. Not found in the United States.

lookalikes.name: Eastern coyote
lookalikes.howToTell: The eastern wolf is larger, but size and colour overlap and hybrids exist; visual identification is unreliable.

lookalikes.name: Grey wolf
lookalikes.howToTell: The eastern wolf is smaller, but it cannot be separated reliably by appearance alone.
